## Theorem: exact core-cylinder union

Let U be the disjoint union of the 11 singleton endpoint germ blocks E_k and V its complement in the original 98-germ carrier. Each strict six-line prefix fixes complementary germ sets a,b partitioning V. Word w sends E_k to A if bit k is 0 and B if 1. For any known depth-five failed core C, set f=C intersect V and m={k:C intersects E_k}. Then C subset A(w) iff f subset a and (w AND m)=0; C subset B(w) iff f subset b and (w AND m)=m. This follows blockwise and preserves original germ identity in C. R303 hereditary failure therefore rejects precisely the union of those cylinders (relative to this particular core dictionary). Grouping cores by identical f, take the bitset union of all their zero-cylinders and one-cylinders separately. The prefix test is then only one subset comparison per side per group, followed by exact 2048-bit union. This is an exact quotient for core-containment observation only, not a quotient of the recursive feasibility relation or of the joint germ state. No new failure claim arises from a miss. For each f group, a mask m contained in m' subsumes the latter cylinder on both sides; explicit minimization is optional since bitset union does it semantically. Construction costs up to 3^11 assignment entries per polarity over all m; group propagation costs at most two fixed-mask tests per active prefix per group plus bitset unions. No wall-time improvement claimed.
